newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer postpones money market fund launch.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer postpones money market fund launch.

text.p: Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Co decided to postpone the launch of a money-market fund planned for early 1997 because the Polish money market is not yet sufficiently developed, Pioneer's deputy president said.
"The money market in Poland is not large enough yet to launch a money market fund now," Larry Wilder told a news conference on Wednesday.

He did not say whether the launch of such a fund would be possible later next year, saying it depended on the development of Polish debt instruments. He added that setting up a money market fund was still one of the company's priorities.

Pioneer deputy president Andrew Gutowski, also present, said the company's Real Estate Fund, which will invest in Polish commercial and residential property, was likely to start operating in the first few months of 1997.
"We believe we will be fully operational by spring 1997," he said.
He said the fund's capital was expected to amount to $50-$60 million and which would have up to 50 investors, would gather its capital in January.
He added that after three years the new fund, set up as a joint stock firm, could be listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.

Pioneer has three open-ended funds: a balanced fund (Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund), a bond fund (Pioneer Interest-Bearing Securities Trust Fund) and a stock fund (Pioneer Aggressive Investment Trust Fund).
It also manages Pioneer Poland Fund, a venture capital fund investing in medium-sized, fast-growing private Polish firms.
Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company is owned by Pioneer Group based in Boston.
